title: Playing at Pete Lala's with Joe Oliver's band, and growing up with Louis Armstrong
summary: He took over Oliver's job at Pete Lala's with a small band including Armstrong, and recalls police stopping the young players and that he and Louis were born in 1900 and went to school together.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Kind of skipping around a little bit. Did you ever work at Pete Lawrence? Yeah, I worked at Pete Lawrence.

When he was at Murray and Iterville. Yeah, I worked there. When I worked there in 19, about 17, 16, I believe in part of 17. How I come to work there, Joe Oliver had the job. Well Joe Oliver went with Ory's band at that time. See, now like Saturday nights and Sunday nights he played with Ory. Well he put me down there, Steve Lewis, Lewis Armstrong, Morris French, you heard of Morris French. Old man Valto, you heard of him, was playing violin. And who was on piano? Well Steve, I told you Steve was on piano. Must have been about four or five pieces.
Well who was in Joe Oliver's band when he was at Pete Lawrence? Old man Valto, he was playing violin.

Is it Freddie Washington piano player? Yeah, Freddie Washington on piano. Who else was on triumphant? I can't say, I'm scared to say. You have to ask Pete, you see. Pete and Manny Manetta, see they can tell you more about it. Because I was a kid, I couldn't go down in the district. When I went down there to play, police stopped me and Lewis two, three times, you know. When they put us in jail, you know. But I told him I had a mother and didn't have no father, you see. And I had to try to help my mother make a living, you see. So he let me slide. Me and Lewis were the youngest one in there, you know. Him and I are the same age, you know. Yeah. He was born in July and I was born in September of 1900. How long have you known him, Louie? All my life. We went to school together, fifth school. I got on Padilla Street. Dated in Franklin. The principal was Arthur P. Williams. Yes, and then Lewis' kids come up together. We born in the third world, him and I both. All in the third world.
